{{Quote|After mating, the H'nemthe females gut the males with those tongues of theirs&mdash;they're as sharp as sword blades, and a lot stronger than they look. Some kind of biological reaction to there being twenty H'nemthe males for every female. The males seem to think it's worth it, to achieve the act of love.|[[Wuher/Legends|Wuher]]|audio=HnemtheFemales-Nightlily.flac|<ref name="Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale">{{StoryCite|story=Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>}}
'''H'nemthe''' were bipedal reptilian [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] with four horns and ridges of bone and skin on their faces. They had long, gently curving noses, three-fingered hands, and pink to blue-gray skin. Their [[H'nemthe/Legends|homeworld]] and [[H'nemthe (language)/Legends|native language]] were also named H'nemthe. The H'nemthe loved the arts, particularly music. They were rarely found off H'nemthe.

H'nemthe society was centered around true love and their unusual mating rituals. Due to a major discrepancy in the number of males compared to females on H'nemthe, the female would kill her mate upon mating. Despite this, the H'nemthe had no reservations about mating, and made finding love the focal point of their culture. Many species saw them as barbaric due to this, although the H'nemthe were otherwise very peaceful.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Universal Truth Number One: You should never say 'Well, why don't you bite my head off?' to a female H'nemthe who is bigger than you are.|[[Kardue'sai'Malloc/Legends|Kardue'sai'Malloc]]|<ref name="Empire Blues: The Devaronian's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=Empire Blues: The Devaronian's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>}}
H'nemthe were [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] reptilians. They had three fingers on their hands, and their skin varied between [[Color/Legends|blue]]-[[Color/Legends|gray]] and pink. They had long noses, [[Color/Legends|green]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], and ridged, bony faces. The average H'nemthe stood 1.7 meters tall, the typical height of a [[Human/Legends|Human]]. H'nemthe were omnivores.<ref name="NEGAS" />

H'nemthe had four small horns, actually sensory cones, on their heads. These cones were used much like the way [[Gotal/Legends|Gotals]] used their cones—to sense electromagnetic fields and weather patterns. Their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] [[H'nemthe/Legends|H'nemthe]] had very unusual and irregular weather patterns due to its three moons. These cones had thus evolved as an adaptation to the extreme weather patterns and variable lighting conditions on H'nemthe, helping them cope with the changing conditions. These cones were also able to sense heat differences in their environment as well as the emotional state of other beings, making them skilled hunters like the Gotals. However, the Gotals were not related to the H'nemthe.<ref name="NEGAS" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Mating is such a solemn thing, such an awe-inspiring thing&hellip;|[[M'iiyoom Onith/Legends|M'iiyoom Onith]]|audio=HnemtheMating-Nightlily.flac|<ref name="Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale" />}}
[[File:Hnemthe.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A H'nemthe in Jabba's Palace]]
The highly structured H'nemthe society was shaped by the natural ratio of the H'nemthe [[Gender/Legends|sexes]]: only one female was born for every twenty males. Despite this imbalance, their culture was based primarily on the search for true love and the creation of new life, which they considered to be the ultimate in spiritual fulfillment.<ref name="NEGAS" />

When a female H'nemthe consummated her relationship with a male, she eviscerated him with her knife-shaped tongue, considering it a proof of love. As a result, male and female H'nemthe mated very rarely, and then only in the case of true love. Since virgin females were rare, they lived a sheltered existence, and were seldom allowed to leave their homeworld. Strict traditions also restricted virgin females to a [[Vegetarian/Legends|vegetarian]] diet, ensuring that their first lover's flesh was the first meat they tasted. The males of the species were timid and spent a considerable amount of their adult lives looking for true love.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Many outsiders considered the deadly H'nemthe mating rituals to be a bizarre contradiction in an otherwise peaceful society. H'nemthe philosophers disagreed, however, pointing out that life coming from [[Death/Legends|death]] was the way of [[The galaxy/Legends|the universe]]. In their beliefs, death was merely a change in form that paved the way for future generations. H'nemthe believed that a male killed after mating would receive the ultimate spiritual reward by going on to the netherworld to act as a spiritual guardian for his offspring, and males were thus unafraid of the certain death that would come their way if they found this love.<ref name="NEGAS" />

H'nemthe prized music, and their music in turn was considered pleasant by non-H'nemthe. They also valued calligraphy, and H'nemthe who had either of these skills were given great accord in their culture. Poetry was also very important to the H'nemthe, and it was traditional for lovers to write each other poems. Females especially were expected to be talented in the arts. H'nemthe also enjoyed sciences and history, and studied them to learn more and prepare themselves for potential leadership opportunities. However, the [[H'nemthe (language)/Legends|H'nemthe spoken language]] was considered unpleasant to outsiders, as it was squeaky.<ref name="NEGAS" />

The H'nemthe had a [[Direct democracy/Legends|direct democracy]] on their [[Planet/Legends|planet]], generally ruled by a female, as the males often had short lifespans due to the H'nemthe mating ritual. A [[Senate]] on H'nemthe consisted of delegates selected by local governments.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Common H'nemthe names included Garriel, H'rassh, Liakkor, S'Basso, Vir'roc and Vishki.<ref name="Ultimate Alien Anthology">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref>

==History==
The planet H'nemthe had few viable exports save for [[Mineral/Legends|minerals]], and though H'nemthe were known to take jobs in the music industry, they rarely left their home planet. They had few visitors and imported little, occasionally trading for technology or [[Starship/Legends|ships]].<ref name="NEGAS" /> When the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Invasion of H'nemthe|took control]] of H'nemthe, many left to join the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] on [[Anoat/Legends|Anoat]].<ref name="CSWE" /> Following the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] made overtures to the H'nemthe leaders in hopes of becoming trading partners with the species.<ref name="NEGAS" /> At some point during the New Republic's rule, the [[Shi'ido]] [[Sentientologist|anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] included an entry on the H'nemthe in his publication ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species" /><ref name="EGAS viii">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], p. viii.</ref>

==H'nemthe in the galaxy==
[[File:Wretched_Hive.png|thumb|right|175px|A H'nemthe in a bar]]
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], a H'nemthe was present on [[Cavamina Minor]], a [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]], when the Jedi [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]] traveled there to capture [[Attuma Duum]].<ref name="Shon-Ju">''[[The Clone Wars: Deadly Hands of Shon-Ju]]''</ref> In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], [[M'iiyoom Onith/Legends|M'iiyoom Onith]] was one of the rare virgin females to leave her homeworld as part of an experiment to see how females would fare in finding a mate not from H'nemthe.<ref name="NEGAS" /> In [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], she fell in love with the Gotal [[Feltipern Trevagg/Legends|Feltipern Trevagg]]. Trevagg, who was was unaware of the nature of H'nemthe mating rituals, seduced Onith, and was killed immediately afterward.<ref name="Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale" /> Onith herself returned to her homeworld, where she gained a certain amount of notoriety. Her mating resulted in no progeny, as the Gotal and H'nemthe species were genetically incompatible.<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Yamnoss]] was present in the same cantina, during a night shift a few months after, when a mandatory curfew was issued by Imperial decree.<ref name="The Star Wars Holiday Special">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref> A [[Unidentified H'nemthe|H'nemthe]] could be found in [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> One H'nemthe, [[Dafi (bounty hunter)|Dafi]], worked as a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] during [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], and was an old rival of the [[Lepi/Legends|Lepi]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Jaxxon/Legends|Jaxxon]]. During a hunt for the Rebel hero [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], Dafi was gunned down by Jaxxon's partner, [[Amaiza Foxtrain/Legends|Amaiza Foxtrain]], on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]].<ref name="TNMS">{{SW|url=news/the-not-so-magnificent-seven|text=The Not-So Magnificent Seven|int=The Not-So Magnificent Seven|nolive=1}}</ref>

[[Unidentified H'nemthe hoodlum|A H'nemthe]] was also a member of [[Spiz's gang]].<ref name="Star Wars: Zam Wesell">''[[Star Wars: Zam Wesell]]''</ref> H'nemthe could also be found working for [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]] as [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] or as suppliers for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].<ref name="Star Wars Customizable Card Game">[[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The H'nemthe were created for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. Their backstory was later expanded on in several books, such as ''[[Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina]]'', [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], and ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''.
